summary: John is born to Elizabeth; when Zacharias writes, “His name is John,” his speech returns, and he prophesies God’s salvation and his son’s calling.
key_insight: After months of silence, Zacharias’s first words are praise, and most of his song is not about his son. He blesses God for raising up “a horn of salvation for us in the house of His servant David” before he says a word about John, and even then John’s task is to go before the Lord.
story: When Elizabeth’s time came, she gave birth to a son. Her neighbors and relatives heard how the Lord had shown great mercy to her, and they rejoiced with her.

On the eighth day they came to circumcise the child, and they were going to name him Zacharias, after his father. But his mother answered, “No; he shall be called John.” They objected, “There is no one among your relatives who is called by this name.” So they made signs to his father to ask what he wanted him called.

Zacharias asked for a writing tablet and wrote, “His name is John.” Everyone marveled. Immediately his mouth was opened and his tongue loosed, and he spoke, praising God. Fear came on all who lived around them, and the news spread through all the hill country of Judea. All who heard it kept it in their hearts and asked, “What kind of child will this be?” For the hand of the Lord was with him.

Then Zacharias was filled with the Holy Spirit and prophesied: “Blessed is the Lord God of Israel, for He has visited and redeemed His people.” God had raised up a horn of salvation in the house of His servant David, as He had promised through His prophets, to save His people from their enemies. He had remembered His holy covenant and the oath He swore to Abraham, so that His people might serve Him without fear, in holiness and righteousness all their days.

Then he turned to his infant son: “And you, child, will be called the prophet of the Highest; for you will go before the face of the Lord to prepare His ways.” John would give God’s people knowledge of salvation by the forgiveness of their sins, through the tender mercy of God, by which the Dayspring from on high has visited us, “to give light to those who sit in darkness and the shadow of death, to guide our feet into the way of peace.”
The child grew and became strong in spirit, and he lived in the deserts until the day he was shown to Israel.

scene.label: The eighth day
scene.text: God commanded that boys be circumcised on the eighth day as the sign of His covenant with Abraham (Genesis 17:12; Leviticus 12:3). Luke shows that the child was also named at that time.

scene.label: A family name
scene.text: Sons were often named after a father or grandfather, so the relatives’ objection was natural. Naming the child John broke with family custom and followed the angel’s word (Luke 1:13).

scene.label: The writing tablet
scene.text: Probably a small wooden board coated with wax, written on with a pointed stylus. The relatives “made signs” to Zacharias, which suggests he could not hear either.

scene.label: Names that tell the story
scene.text: Zacharias means the LORD remembers, and the song says God acted “to remember His holy covenant.” Elizabeth can mean my God is an oath, and the song recalls “the oath which He swore.” John means the LORD is gracious. The family’s names tell the story Zacharias sings.

scene.label: The Dayspring
scene.text: The word means the rising of the sun. The prophets pictured the Messiah’s coming as dawn for people in darkness (Isaiah 9:2; Malachi 4:2). In the Greek Old Testament the same word also translates “Branch,” the prophets’ name for the coming King from David’s line (Jeremiah 23:5).

witnesses.luke: Only Luke tells of John’s birth, and he sets it beside Jesus’ birth in the next chapter: two births, two namings, two songs of praise. He ends with John growing up in the wilderness, where the word of God will later come to him (Luke 3:2), and his father’s prophecy has already told readers what John’s work will be.

seeing.reveals: Zacharias’s song centers on Jesus: the horn of salvation from David’s house, the Dayspring from on high who visits people sitting in darkness. John is the prophet; Jesus is the Lord whose ways he prepares.
seeing.living: Zacharias’s tongue was loosed the moment he obeyed, writing the name the angel gave even against his family’s wishes. His first use of his restored voice was to bless God. When God keeps a promise you once doubted, let gratitude be the first thing you say.
seeing.ponder: What promise has God kept in your life that you have not yet stopped to bless Him for?

preaching.big_idea: God remembers His promises, and His mercy dawns like sunrise on people sitting in darkness.
outline: A name that obeyed the word (59–66)
A child sent ahead of the dawn (76–80)
preaching.watch_for: The word “visited” frames the song. God “has visited and redeemed His people” (1:68), and “the Dayspring from on high has visited us” (1:78). God’s visit in Jesus is the theme from start to finish.
